mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% (FEDFUNDS < 3.0%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns. This signal is always active without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 3.0% in 60% of the next 5 years, but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 255.0) signals potential monetary tightening and increased risk aversion, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns. The signal activates when CPIAUCSL exceeds 255.0.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 255.0 in 60% of the next 5 years, but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high unemployment (UNRATE > 4.0%) and declining industrial production (INDPRO < 108.0) signal an emerging recession, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings and increased risk aversion. The signal requires joint behavior of both series.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.0 AND INDPRO < 108.0 in 60% of the next 5 years, but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 255.0) causes negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to rising real interest rates and reduced risk appetite. The signal requires joint behavior of both series to activate.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.0 AND CPIAUCSL > 255.0 in 60% of the next 5 years, but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS > 500000.0) indicate robust consumer demand, supporting corporate earnings and producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns. This signal is always active without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 500000.0 in 60% of the next 5 years, but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 108.0) signals weakening supply chain activity and reduced economic output, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to lower corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 108.0 in 60% of the next 5 years, but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 4.0%) signals economic weakness and increased risk aversion, causing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns. The signal activates when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.0 in 60% of the next 5 years, but 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 108.0) signals weakening economic activity, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings growth and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 108.0 in 60% of the next 5 years, but 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.
